solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fantastic being nipped by ferret!

parts.note: a hob is a male ferret
bit is the past tense of bite, to nip

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a fantastic creature that has been bitten by a ferret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' here means next to, with the pieces listed in the opposite order to the answer. 'Fantastic' looks like praise but belongs to the definition: a being from fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's small furry-footed folk are creatures of fantasy fiction, so one is a fantastic being.

clue.text: No hunter is disturbed when being chased

indicators.note: disturbed means moved out of place, so the letters of no hunter are mixed up

explanation.surface: A huntsman is not bothered while the quarry is pursued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No hunter' looks like a statement about the chase, but its letters are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the run is fleeing from pursuers, so being chased.

clue.text: Row breaks out after being discovered as insolvent

parts.note: a bank is a row or tier, as of keys or oars

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: a fight that breaks out erupts

explanation.surface: An argument flares up when someone is found to be broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a quarrel in the surface but a line here. 'discovered' strips the outer E and S from ERUPTS to leave RUPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankrupt means legally declared unable to pay one's debts, so insolvent.

clue.text: Change class after one leaves train station's opening

indicators.note: after means the word for class is placed following the earlier pieces
leaves means goes away from, so a letter drops out of the word train

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word station's

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Someone changes class once a passenger alights at the station entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one leaves' takes the I out of 'train'; 'opening' and 'after' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform something is to change its form or nature completely.

clue.text: Greek characters crush destructive aquatic mammal

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter; more than one are mus
to quash a revolt is to crush it

explanation.surface: Letters of the Greek alphabet seem to flatten a harmful water animal.
explanation.walkthrough: MUS is the plural of the Greek letter mu.
explanation.definitionFit: Musquash is another name for the muskrat, a water rodent known for damaging riverbanks and crops.

clue.text: HMI, when expanded literally, could become mediocre

parts.note: H is the middle letter of the word the, and MI stands for the M1, Britain's best-known motorway or road

explanation.surface: Spelling out a school inspector's initials yields something unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: HMI is Her Majesty's Inspector of schools, but 'expanded literally' it reads as H, the middle of THE, plus MI, the M1 motorway: a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road describes something unadventurous and moderate, so average or mediocre.

clue.text: Arrow causing dispute

definitions.meaning: a short heavy bolt shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: An arrow sets off an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a square-headed crossbow bolt and, separately, an argument between people.

clue.text: Twice old flier is confused by a wing's cross-section

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so all these letters are jumbled together
twice means the letter for old is used two times

explanation.surface: An elderly pilot gets befuddled by a wing diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice old' gives OO, which 'is confused' with FLIER and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerofoil is the curved shape of a wing seen in section, designed to generate lift.

clue.text: In period when school finishes

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a period is a span of time

explanation.surface: Part of the school day as the lessons end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a preposition in the surface but means at home here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hometime is the moment at the end of the school day when pupils leave.

clue.text: Flag of Laurel and ultimately Hardy essentially

parts.note: Stan was the first name of Laurel of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word and
essentially means the essence, the inner letters of Hardy without its ends

explanation.surface: A banner belonging to the comedy pair Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' gives his first name, STAN. 'ultimately' takes D, the last letter of 'and', and 'essentially' takes ARD, the middle of 'Hardy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or flag, such as a royal or regimental one.

clue.text: Little dog has strange lip

parts.note: a lab is a shortened labrador, so the dog name is made little
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A small dog has an odd-looking lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened name: LAB for labrador.
explanation.definitionFit: A labrum is an anatomical lip or lip-like edge, for example on an insect's mouth or a joint socket.

clue.text: Agent rails frantically as an act of retaliation

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: doing something frantically is doing it wildly, so the word rails is jumbled

explanation.surface: A furious agent rants wildly in revenge for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rails' is a verb in the surface, to rant; here its letters are shuffled to give RISAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is a retaliatory act, revenge taken for an injury suffered.

clue.text: Advantage for female with you know what!

parts.note: pro is Latin for in favour of, so for
it is the coy word for something left unnamed, especially sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that a woman gains from something unmentionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you know what' is a nudge-nudge euphemism, IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is gain or benefit, so an advantage obtained from something.

clue.text: It's the custom for most of troops to reassemble in front of column

indicators.note: in front of means the reshuffled letters come ahead of the abbreviation for column
to reassemble is to put back together in a new arrangement, so the letters are shuffled
most of means the word troops loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers regrouping at the head of a column of marchers is the usual practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final S from 'troops' before 'to reassemble' shuffles what is left; 'in front of' places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the established code of procedure, the accepted custom on formal occasions.

clue.text: Conservative, not Liberal political bust skull bone

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the altered letters are scrambled
Conservative, not Liberal means one party letter stands in place of the other

explanation.surface: A Tory-not-Liberal political statue is in fact a head bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' swaps an L in POLITICAL for C, giving POCITICAL, which 'bust' rearranges. 'bust' looks like a sculpted head, fitting the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The occipital is the bone forming the back and base of the skull.

clue.text: Bird in difficulty

definitions.meaning: a wading bird of the sandpiper family
a tangle or problem, as in a knotty issue

explanation.surface: A bird finds itself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sandpiper-like wader and also a tangle or intricate problem, as in tying oneself in knots.

clue.text: Cardigan maybe, where fool is said to be on river

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed on top of the next piece
is said means spoken aloud, so the word for fool is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a fool supposedly sits beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is said' signals the homophone and 'on' stacks it above the river in this down clue; the Wear flows through Durham in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is one kind of garment made of knitted wool, so an example of the category.

clue.text: Kiss large copper recently!

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, large
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to kiss a big policeman who arrived just now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but here it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word for to kiss.

clue.text: This fruit grows in the end all over on a regular basis

indicators.note: in the end picks out the final letter of the word grows
on a regular basis takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of all over

explanation.surface: A fruit that eventually spreads everywhere, time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives S from 'grows'; 'on a regular basis' gives L, O, E from the even letters of 'all over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloe is the small sour blue-black fruit of the blackthorn, used to flavour gin.

clue.text: Do they slink about wearing these?

definitions.text: Do they slink about wearing these?

parts.words: Do they slink about wearing these?
parts.note: soft rubber-soled shoes make no noise, and those who creep about stealthily could also be called by the same word

explanation.surface: A question whether prowlers move quietly in particular shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The word works twice: the soft shoes, and people who sneak, who would choose them.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-soled canvas trainers are silent underfoot, ideal footwear for creeping about unheard.

clue.text: One eats everything micro oven cooked except for carrot top

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or worked over, so the letters of micro oven are rearranged
top means the first letter of the word carrot

explanation.surface: Someone eats anything zapped in a microwave, except the carrot leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for' removes C, the 'top' of carrot, from MICRO OVEN; 'cooked' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore is an animal or person that feeds on both plants and meat, so anything at all.

clue.text: Electronic proposal includes constant smiley face perhaps

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting
c is the symbol for a constant in maths, and for the speed of light

explanation.surface: An online suggestion that keeps showing a smiling face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts C inside MOTION, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face is one example of the little symbols typed into messages to show feelings.

clue.text: Former thespian is one demanding rights

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A retired actor now claims what he believes he is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand payment or compliance, so an exactor insists on dues and rights.

clue.text: President coming across as honest fellow

indicators.note: coming across as means sounding like, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: an honest fellow is a true man

explanation.surface: A head of state who appears to be a decent, honest man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming across as' signals a homophone: 'true man' sounds like the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S Truman was the 33rd President of the United States, from 1945 to 1953.

clue.text: Stress shown by European associated with awkward mishaps

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or ill-fitting, so the word mishaps is rearranged

explanation.surface: A European is under strain because of a series of clumsy accidents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' shuffles 'mishaps' to PHASIS, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress laid on a word or point to mark it as important.

clue.text: Speed backwards then finally adopt serene ballet position

indicators.note: backwards means the word for speed is read from the end

parts.note: to race is to speed

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the words adopt and serene

explanation.surface: A dancer rushes back, then calmly strikes a graceful ballet pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns RACE into ECAR; 'finally' takes T and E, the ends of 'adopt' and 'serene'.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet, écarté is a position with the body angled to the audience and one leg extended.

clue.text: Working at article with patient one described in book

parts.note: on can mean at, as in on time or on the spot
the is the definite article
Job is the long-suffering hero of the Book of Job in the Bible, proverbially patient

explanation.surface: A care worker attends to a patient written up in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' is a hospital patient in the surface, but here means long-suffering: the patience of Job is proverbial.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the job means at work, busy with one's task.

clue.text: Whisky money gets us staple food

parts.note: rye is a whisky distilled from rye grain
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash from whisky buys us our basic groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money' is BREAD in slang, which hides the fact that the answer is bread of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made with rye flour is a basic everyday food in much of northern Europe.

clue.text: Final edition survived

parts.note: last means final

explanation.surface: The last printing of something managed to survive.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lasted is to have endured or carried on, so to have survived.
